transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Well, I'm here because for a really long time now, my sleep has just been broken. I mean, I fall into bed absolutely exhausted, but then I wake up to every little sound in the house. And then I'm always up before my alarm even goes off, just feeling like I never really rested at all.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Yeah, I suppose I have. Most days it just feels like... well, like the color has gone out of things. Even when I'm sitting at Sunday dinner with my family, or just looking at art I used to really enjoy, it all just feels flat. And honestly, I find myself having to work really hard not to tear up, and there's not even a clear reason for it.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?
No, I don't think so. I haven't really noticed any problems with my focus. I can still pay attention to things and get my work done just fine, even with being so tired. My concentration seems okay.
Have you been feeling this down nearly every day for at least two weeks?

Yes, definitely. Actually, it's been much longer than two weeks. It's... well, this has been going on nearly every day since my mother-in-law moved in with us. That was a little over two years ago now.
During these past two years, have there been any stretches of at least two months when you were not feeling depressed most days?

No, I don't think so. There really hasn't been a break like that. I mean, I might have a decent day here and there, but... no, definitely not two whole months where I felt okay. It's just been this way pretty much the whole time.
Have you been feeling badly about yourself?

No, I wouldn't say so. I don't really have negative feelings about myself. I mean, I know I work hard and I'm doing the best I can to take care of my family... I'm just down all the time. But I don't feel worthless or bad about who I am, if that's what you mean.
Aside from feeling sleepy from poor sleep, have you been feeling low on energy most days?

Yes, definitely. By the time I finish seeing my home-health clients for the day and come back to help out at home, my body just feels... heavy. It's like even doing simple things, like charting my notes for work or just folding the laundry, it can feel like it's just too much to push through. I'm just drained.
During this two-year period, was there ever a time when your depression became clearly worse than your usual baseline for at least two weeks?

No, not really. It's... it's just been pretty steady. I mean, I have bad days, sure, but I haven't had a time where it suddenly got a lot worse and stayed that way for a couple of weeks. It's just been this same constant, low feeling pretty much the whole time.

latest_inference.note: Chronic depressed mood for >2 years without any 2-month symptom-free interval supports persistent depressive disorder. No clearly worse >=2-week period argues against superimposed major depressive episodes, so F33.9 and F32.9 are ruled out. Insomnia appears secondary to the mood disorder rather than primary, making F51.0/G47.0 less likely; anxiety disorder not supported.
